_comment: Status overlay for the implementation tracker. backlog.json owns the stories and their acceptance criteria; this file owns delivery status, the abridged title shown in the tracker, and phase alignment. Regenerate the page with `npm run tracker`. test/tracker.spec.ts fails if the two files fall out of sync.

platform_milestones.name: Cloud staging foundation
platform_milestones.note: The repository now supports pooled managed PostgreSQL with verified TLS, staging configuration fail-closed rules, public liveness/readiness probes, graceful shutdown, structured request telemetry, a non-root immutable container, Kubernetes TLS/secret manifests, and CI publish/deploy workflows. The staging Kustomize bundle rendered successfully, and Docker built and ran the production image as a healthy non-root container with a read-only root filesystem and passing liveness/readiness checks.
platform_milestones.remaining: Not cloud-activated: choose AWS/Azure/GCP, provision the managed database/cluster/DNS/secret binding, then prove HTTPS, backup restore and image rollback in that account.

US16.4.name: Per-twin persistent FIFO queue
US16.4.note: Verified by test/us16.4-16.5.spec.ts — inbound records and outbound state writes are persisted before execution, partitioned by immutable twin identity, assigned durable queue positions and claimed atomically. A twin head executes in order while unrelated twins proceed independently; expired claims resume from the original position without replaying settled work.

US16.5.name: Twin-level failure isolation
US16.5.note: Verified by test/us16.4-16.5.spec.ts — exhausted ingestion, transformation and provider-write failures pause only their twin partition. Tenant-scoped twin-DLQ endpoints expose the payload, error and attempt history and re-inject corrected payloads at the original FIFO position.

US17.1.name: Native connectors, discovery and ingestion
US17.1.note: Verified by test/us17.1.spec.ts and the browser smoke suite against deterministic Jira Cloud REST v3 and ServiceNow Table API fakes: reference-only credentials, a live-HTTP guard, native project/table, field, custom-field and state discovery, capability limitations that block activation, watermarked paginated ingestion into canonical twins with immutable correlation nodes, echo-suppressed US13.1 state propagation and retried connector work orders. Partial: Azure DevOps, Zendesk, Salesforce, GitHub and Asana adapters, webhook-triggered ingestion, and validation against a live Jira/ServiceNow tenant remain.

US17.2.name: Visual mappings with sandboxed scripts
US17.2.note: Versioned, tenant-scoped field mapping definitions (draft/published/superseded) with direct, constant, value-table, conditional and scripted rules, evaluated by a pure translator and validated against discovered target schemas and a nesting-depth cap at save time. Scripts run in a genuine V8 isolate (isolated-vm, not Node's vm) under a real 500ms wall-clock timeout, a real heap-memory limit, zero ambient globals, and a fresh isolate per call. Wired into the same durable FIFO work-order pipeline as US13.1 state translation: one composite work order carries whichever of state and mapped fields actually changed, echo suppression extends to the mapped field set, and schema drift or an unmapped value holds the whole work order rather than partially writing it. Jira and ServiceNow adapters and their sandboxes accept field-plus-state or fields-only writes. Operators edit any explicitly write-back-enabled field as free text or a picklist in the twin drawer, routed through the same governed connector work order as a state change. A visual field-mapping studio (value-table and conditional rule builders, plus a script editor) mirrors the existing state-mapping studio. Verified by test/us17.2.spec.ts (definitions, publish-time validation, and the full propagation pipeline), test/mapping-script-sandbox.spec.ts (real timeout/memory kills, capability absence, a vm-escape attempt, oversized/malformed/deeply-nested output), and 3 new browser tests at desktop and 390px.

US17.3.name: Scheduled native-query triggers
US17.3.note: Verified by test/us17.3.spec.ts and a browser test against deterministic Jira and ServiceNow fakes: JQL and ServiceNow encoded queries are validated, saved as drafts, published and run on a per-query schedule; each run enqueues the matching records changed since the query's own watermark through the existing durable ingestion queue, deduplicated, with the watermark committed in the same transaction. A query that would read without bound (no selective scope on every OR/NQ branch, its own ORDER BY, or a filter on the managed watermark field) is blocked at publish with an actionable error naming the clause to add, and is re-checked on every run. Runs use a database lease, back off on provider failure and resume across pages. Partial: WIQL is syntax- and scope-validated only, because no Azure DevOps adapter exists to run it; the unbounded-scan check is a static heuristic that cannot see a real instance's indexes; and nothing has run against a live Jira or ServiceNow tenant.

US17.4.name: Bulk synchronization and historical backfill
US17.4.note: A backfill job is a validated time range split into persisted, half-open chunks that partition it exactly, read page by page from Jira or ServiceNow through the connector's own scope and any operator query checked like a scheduled one. Each page commits atomically with its chunk progress, per-record audit rows and durable ingestion-queue entries, so a crash, pause or takeover resumes from the saved page and nothing is read twice or lost. Adaptive control halves concurrency and adds delay (honouring Retry-After) on throttling or transient failure, grows it again on sustained success up to the job maximum, and paces every request through one shared per-minute ceiling; one job runs per connector at a time. A failing chunk fails alone and can be retried. Processed, queued and failed counts are read from the real queue, and a CSV audit report (one row per record, linked twin, queue status, failed chunks, formula-safe, with the export itself audited) is available through the API and a studio dialog. A general stale-version guard now stops an older record from overwriting a newer twin. Verified by test/us17.4.spec.ts (35 tests) and a browser test against deterministic Jira and ServiceNow fakes, with throttle feedback, the pacer and the cancel guard each confirmed to fail when deliberately broken. Not yet run against a live Jira or ServiceNow tenant, so real provider throttling behaviour is unobserved.

US20.1.note: New from the master backlog. No Chrome/Edge extension shows twin status or RBAC-gated resync and unlink actions on native ticket pages.

US20.2.name: Connector-led management workspace
US20.2.note: Verified by test/us20.2.spec.ts and the connector-led browser suite (sandbox providers). CADENA_INTERACTION_MODE selects connector-led (staging/production default), pilot (local only) or standalone. Connector-led mode opens on source health, lag, twin counts and write-back queues with Connect / Discover / Synchronize as primary actions, and refuses local creation and backlog import server-side. Twins show source, native link, sync state, last success, field authority and counterparts. Externally owned fields are read-only unless a permitted outbound mapping exists; permitted state changes become audited connector work orders, and blocked edits are audited and explained. Twin-backed WorkItem projection (test/twin-projection.spec.ts) now places connector twins under the SLA, escalation-notification, traceability and flow-metrics engines, with source-owned fields read-only and state changes routed through governed write-back.

US10.9.name: Authenticated tenant and actor identity
US10.9.note: Verified by test/us10.9.spec.ts — bearer credentials stored only as a SHA-256 hash, tenant resolved from the credential, a contradicting header refused, revocation honoured, and credential management restricted to admins. Header identity survives only behind CADENA_ALLOW_HEADER_AUTH for development.
